findings.title: 15 tap target(s) smaller than M3's comfortable 48×48px at 375px wide
findings.description: 15 tap target(s) smaller than M3's comfortable 48×48px at 375px wide — they clear the WCAG 2.5.8 24px minimum (2 via the spacing/inline exception). Examples: a.sr-only.focus:not-sr-only "Skip to content" (1×1px); a.font-semibold.text-navy "Cense" (42×18px); button.no-print.flex "Hide dollar amounts" (44×44px). Measured at the 375×812px mobile viewport.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the control or add padding so its hit area is at least 48×48px.

findings.recommendation: Consolidate to a small token set: define CSS variables for the sanctioned values and replace ad-hoc ones.

findings.title: 1 animation/transition(s) under 50ms (non-instant but too fast to read).
findings.description: 1 animation/transition(s) under 50ms (non-instant but too fast to read). Examples: *, ::after, ::before.
findings.recommendation: Keep animation durations within the 50–1000ms scale — long enough to read, short enough to feel responsive.

findings.title: 1 transition(s) animate layout props (width/height/top/left/margin)
findings.description: 1 transition(s) animate layout props (width/height/top/left/margin) — animate transform/opacity instead (jank). Examples: .transition-\[width\].
findings.recommendation: Animate transform/opacity instead of layout properties (width/height/top/left/margin) to avoid jank.

findings.title: 1 infinite decorative loop(s)
findings.description: 1 infinite decorative loop(s) — reserve infinite motion for progress indicators. Examples: .animate-pulse.
findings.recommendation: Reserve infinite animation for progress indicators; give decorative loops a finite iteration count.

notAutoDetectable: Spatial coherence — whether elements enter/exit from where they logically belong (a menu growing from its anchor, a sheet rising from the edge it docks to). The audit sees durations and easings, not spatial origin.
Clean fades — whether opacity transitions are free of mid-fade color shifts, banding, or double-compositing. Only a human eye (or pixel diff) can judge fade quality.
Jump cuts — abrupt state changes with no transition where one is expected (content swaps, route changes). Absence of animation is not itself in the DOM.
Unified direction — whether a group of elements animates along a consistent axis/choreography rather than each doing its own thing.
Perceived hierarchy / emphasis — whether motion draws the eye to the right thing at the right time.
Content-appropriate personality — expressive vs. standard scheme being the right call for the brand and context.
Interruptibility & continuity — whether in-flight animations respond gracefully to new input rather than snapping.
Real contrast under imagery/gradients — text over photos or gradient backgrounds (the audit samples solid computed backgrounds only).
Closed shadow roots — their internals are structurally unreachable from script and are not scanned.
